text:
Jess: Customer reports SSE stream silently stalls then EOF when phone switches from 5G -> WiFi. Happens ~20-40s after network flip. Case 9876, request id 33f7. Logs below.

Omar: Can you grab the client's keepalive settings? Sounds like a TCP idle/keepalive race or token refresh race.

Jess: Minimal repro they used (curl):
```
curl -N -H 'Authorization: Bearer <redacted>' https://api.redwood.com/v1/stream
```
They say stream pauses, then later we get a termination. Edge logs:```
[edge cb2] 2024-09-14T04:12:21Z conn=0x7f8c: write error: EOF
[edge cb2] 2024-09-14T04:12:21Z client 10.1.2.3 -> closed (ECONNRESET)
```

Ryan: That write EOF + ECONNRESET looks like our proxy tearing the connection when mid-handshake for a routed fallback. Mobile OSes also sometimes stop sending keepalives during interface change. Do we see fallback/reroute at the same time?

Nicole: Console shows a routing fallback for that tenant (us-west-2 -> us-east-1) exactly at 2024-09-14T04:12:20Z. I suspect active stream didn't survive the TLS rehandshake.

Jess: Customer uses okhttp SSE on Android 12, keepAlive interval set to 20s. No explicit app-level ping. Token refresh every 15m.

Omar: Repro checklist I want: 1) start SSE in hotspot mode, 2) toggle wifi off/on, 3) capture tcpdump + app logs. Also try adding an app-level ping to confirm.

Jess: Repro steps they provided: 1) start stream, 2) toggle wifi, 3) see partial chunk then silent pause, then final event: 'error: connection aborted'. Example client log:```
I/System.out: SSE: received "data: { partial chunk }"
I/System.out: network: interface change detected
I/System.out: SSE: no data for 25s
I/System.out: SSE: connection aborted by server
```

support-bot: Created internal ticket INC-12987 and linked to support case 9876. Diagnostics bundle: https://redwood.inc/diag/INC-12987 :white_check_mark:

Ryan: Quick workaround for them: enable socket-level keepalive and schedule a small ping every 10-12s. For okhttp: set `socket.setKeepAlive(true)` and do periodic `client.newCall(pingReq).execute()` or use WebSocket pings if available. Server-side, we can add a short grace window so routing fallback doesn't RST active SSEs immediately.

Omar: Also enable extra edge traces for that tenant: set DD_EDGE_CONN_DEBUG=true for 1 hour so we can correlate. I'll open a PR for a temporary grace override.

Nicole: I pulled metrics — small spike in edge 503s at the same minute. Seems correlated with a transient regional routing flaps.

Jess: Customer applied the client ping workaround and reported no disconnects for 45 minutes of aggressive roaming. They asked if platform can do better.

Ryan: Action items: (1) infra: add 30s soft-grace for active SSE during routing fallback (Omar, ETA 3 business days), (2) eng-runtime: investigate why we RST streams on interface-change path (Ryan), (3) support: monitor customer for 24h and escalate if they reoccur (Jess).

Omar: I'll own the infra change and post the PR link when ready.

Jess: Thanks — updating case 9876 with workaround and leaving open for 24h monitoring.

Nicole: marking logs & diag link on the ticket.

Ryan: If anyone wants to reproduce quickly, here's a tiny curl repro that toggles netns on linux and leaves ping enabled:```
# start stream in netns A
ip netns exec A curl -N -H 'Authorization: Bearer <token>' https://api.redwood.com/v1/stream
# move veth to netns B (simulate handoff)
```
Note: requires elevated privileges.

Jess: Closing triage for now, keeping ticket open until customer confirms 24h stable. :thumbsup:
